discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
subfield: Condensed matter physics - topological quantum matter
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological phase, the quantum spin Hall insulator, classified by a Z2 invariant, and Kane with Fu extended this to three-dimensional topological insulators. In 2007 Molenkamp's group observed quantized edge conduction in HgTe quantum wells, the first experimental realization, achieved through outstanding materials growth and nanofabrication. Together these works opened a new field: symmetry-protected topological phases of electronic matter. The field now spans topological superconductors, Weyl semimetals, and the quantum anomalous Hall effect, and it reshaped how we classify band structures. It also shows a close interplay between theory and experiment, from abstract topology to a measured conductance of 2e^2/h. The concepts are deep and have been confirmed in many materials, which puts this among the most consequential advances in condensed matter physics of the past two decades.
